data.name: Lunaria
data.gender_notes: Lunaria is used as a unisex name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Latin word 'lunaris', meaning 'pertaining to the moon'. In ancient Rome, Lunaria was the name of the goddess of the moon. This name has a rich cultural history and can be a beautiful choice for a little girl. The name Lunaria carries the meaning “Moon goddess” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Hebrew, Greek. Parents who choose Lunaria usually hope their child will grow to embody moon goddess and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes the power and mystery of the moon and the natural world.
data.etymology: Lunaria belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Moon goddess.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Lunaria total 4, giving a life-path number of 4. Number 4 is linked with Rahu and with the qualities of stability, discipline and hard work.

data.cultural_impact: The name Lunaria holds a strong cultural significance with its Roman origins, evoking the mystical and magical associations of the lunar goddess. It is a name rooted in history and ancient traditions, offering a connection to the past. For parents seeking a name with a rich cultural background, Lunaria could be a compelling option.
data.spiritual_significance: As the name of a goddess in ancient Roman religion, Lunaria holds a deeper spiritual significance. The Goddess of the Moon was believed to govern cycles of growth and change and was honored for her nurturing and protective qualities. This name can be seen as a reminder of the ever-changing cycles of life and the power of the divine in guiding us through life's corridors. For parents seeking to give their child a name with a profound spiritual meaning, Lunaria is an option packed with symbolism and rich historical significance.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Lunaria, derived from the Latin word for "moon," represents the divine feminine and the cycles of life. It embodies the nurturing, intuitive, and mysterious aspects of the moon, inspiring inner growth and connection to the natural world.

historical_references.reference: Lunaria, the Roman goddess of the Moon, was often identified with the Greek goddess Selene. Both were associated with the cycles of the moon and the changing of the seasons.
historical_references.time_period: Classical antiquity, 1st century BC - 5th century AD

historical_references.reference: During the Middle Ages, a Christian nun named Lunatilla or Lunaria is said to have lived in the 6th century in the monastery of San Vincenzo al Volturno in Italy. She is believed to have been a hermit and possessed the gifts of healing and prophecy.

modern_usage.modern_context: The Christian name 'Lunaria' is increasingly used in modern contexts related to astrology, spirituality, and wicca practices. On Instagram, Lunaria is tagged in posts about lunar phases, moon rituals, and astrology. On Pinterest, there are boards dedicated to Lunaria, moon magic, and lunar cycles. On TikTok, #lunaria hashtag shows videos about moon phases, astrology, and moon rituals, as well as personal experiences and reflections. Overall, Lunaria represents the feminine, nurturing, and intuitive aspects of the moon and is often associated with the spiritual journey, self-care, and personal growth.

name_in_real_life.story: A devoted Christian named Hannah Lunaria in Rome, Italy credits much of their spiritual journey to their name Lunaria, which means "Moon goddess". They believe their name has been a blessing and reminder of God's presence in their life.
